title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-15
content:
Summary:
- Today noticed ~20-30% throughput regression on C4-reserved pool since 2026-02-18 deploy (traffic pattern: short requests, median seq len ~64). Latency P50 stable, P95 increased slightly but within SLO. Total tokens/sec dropped across steady load test (k6 synthetic) and production spike synthetic traffic.

What I observed:
- Regression surfaced after rotuine runtime kernel selection change (PR #789) which changed default batching window heuristics and introduced per-model batch-window override.
- A/B showed new runtime = lower throughput when request sizes are small and concurrency high.
- KV cache hit rate dropped from ~0.62 to ~0.15 for affected model (gpt-open-13b-q8).

Commands tried / reproduction steps (local cluster):
1) Baseline run (pre-PR behavior):
- start local runtime with pinned old-image tag: ./deploy/local/run.sh --image runtime:2026-02-10 --pool c4-small
- load test: k6 run small-requests.js --vus 200 --duration 5m
- collected metrics (prometheus): nginx_requests_total, runtime_batches_total, kv_cache_hits_total

2) New-image run (regression):
- ./deploy/local/run.sh --image runtime:main --pool c4-small
- k6 run small-requests.js --vus 200 --duration 5m

3) Debug probes executed:
- curl -sS localhost:8080/metrics | grep runtime_batch_window
  -> runtime_batch_window_seconds{model="gpt-open-13b-q8"} 0.050
- curl -sS localhost:8080/metrics | grep kv_cache_enabled
  -> kv_cache_enabled{model="gpt-open-13b-q8"} 0
- runtime admin: /admin/cache/status -> shows cache shards not reattached after model reload

4) Forcing old batch window via env override:
- RUNTIME_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=20 ./deploy/local/run.sh --image runtime:main --pool c4-small
- Result: throughput recovered ~12% but not fully to baseline. KV cache still low.

Observed logs / error snippets:
- worker-1 | WARN 2026-02-18T14:12:05Z kernel_selector: selected kernel v2 for seq_len_distribution mismatch
- worker-2 | ERROR 2026-02-18T14:12:06Z kvcache: shard attach failed: "no-compatible-backend" (attempt 3)
- worker-2 | INFO 2026-02-18T14:12:07Z kvcache: reinit complete, but sticky_shard_map != expected_shard_map
- router | WARN 2026-02-18T14:12:10Z batching: batch flush triggered by timeout (50ms) with size=1

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Primary hypothesis: per-model batch-window default change increased batch flush timeout to 50ms for small-request workloads -> increases number of small batches and reduces batching efficiency. Combined with malformed shard map prevents KV cache reuse -> throughput drops significantly.
2) Secondary hypothesis: kernel selector change (PR #789) picks a kernel variant that has worse throughput at short seq lengths (cache unfriendly) causing increased per-token time even if single-request latency not huge.
3) Tertiary: autoscaling/placement change causes requests to land on nodes missing kv cache shards (attachment races), causing extra cold-cache penalty. Errors show 'no-compatible-backend' during shard attach.

Quick experiments and results:
- Force batch window to 20ms (env override) -> throughput +12%, kv cache hit rate unchanged. Suggests batch window is part of issue but not sole cause.
- Restart runtime with explicit cache warmup script (preload prefixes) -> kv cache hit rate rose to ~0.55 and throughput recovered to ~95% baseline. Confirms cache attachment/warmup important.
- Rollback kernel-selector to old strategy (local build) -> small throughput improvement (~6%) but still below baseline if kv cache cold.

Interim mitigating actions applied to prod (canary first):
- Rollback per-model batch-window override to previous default (hotfix) and bounced canary nodes. Observed immediate improvement in batching sizes (avg batch size increased from 1.3 -> 2.1) and throughput +15% on canary.
- Add cache-warmup at model load for dedicated pools (short-term): run preload job that sends synthetic prefix traffic to populate shards. This recovered throughput on older nodes.

Root-cause candidate (working):
- Combination of: change in default batch-window heuristics + a regression in shard attach logic introduced in the same release. The two together turn small-request traffic into a high-rate of tiny batches and prevent KV cache reuse, amplifying perf impact.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did shard attach fail intermittently during rolling deploy? Race in placement / backend discovery or subtle API change in shard registry? Need to inspect service discovery logs.
- Are there more models affected or only gpt-open-13b-q8 family? Quick telemetry suggests models with heavier KV-dependency (longer contexts) show bigger impact.
- Why did kernel selector pick v2 kernel for short seqs? Need to review selector heuristics and recorded seq_len_distribution input.

Next steps / TODO (owners assigned inline):
- [Ethan] Full fuzz test for shard attach under rolling deploys (linear INF-342).
- [Priya] Rework batch-window rollout flag: make default conservative + expose per-deployment feature flagging.
- [Samira] Add integration test that simulates cold-warm kv cache transitions and verifies throughput thresholds.
- [Infra] Add extra logging to shard registry agent to capture attachment failure context (timeout, backend list, discovery response).

Notes to self / reminders:
- Ticket: INF-342 (investigation) - link above.
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime - thread ts 1676601234567. Pinged infra and SRE for placement logs.
- Keep canary rollback ready in case the hotfix doesn't hold under production burst.

Potential follow-ups for product/console team:
- Expose "batching efficiency" metric in Console (avg batch size by route + batch-window setting) so customers can see impact of overrides.
- Add rollout checklist item: verify kv cache attachments on new nodes before shifting traffic (automate with readiness probe).

Timestamped breadcrumb log (short):
- 2026-02-18 14:05: first 5% canary alerts for throughput regression
- 2026-02-18 14:12: observed kvcache attach errors in canary logs
- 2026-02-18 14:30: started local reproduction (samira)
- 2026-02-18 15:10: forced batch window override -> partial recovery
- 2026-02-19 09:00: applied batch-window rollback to canary -> positive signal
- 2026-02-20 10:00: deployed cache-warmup job to affected pool -> throughput near baseline

If any of the above experiments are flaky, capture raw prometheus query results:
- rate(runtime_batches_total[2m])
- avg by (model) (rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / max(1, rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))

Appendix (quick commands to reproduce locally):
- build: make build-runtime && docker tag runtime:local runtime:main
- run old image: ./deploy/local/run.sh --image runtime:2026-02-10 --pool c4-small
- run new image: RUNTIME_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=50 ./deploy/local/run.sh --image runtime:main --pool c4-small
- k6 script: small-requests.js (attached to linked PR in GH)

-- end of scratchpad --
